subject: Nitric acid
hook: NITRIC ACID IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Nitric acid was described in Arabic alchemical texts as early as the 8th century, centuries before the commonly cited 13th‑century European discovery
angle_support: According to Eric John Holmyard and Ahmad Y. al‑Hassan, nitric acid was also referenced in various earlier Arabic works such as the Ṣundūq al‑ḥikma ('Chest of Wisdom') attributed to Jabir ibn Hayyan (8th century)...

The discovery of mineral acids such as nitric acid is generally presumed to go back to 13th‑century European alchemy... However, according to ... nitric acid was also referenced in ... 8th‑century Arabic works.
title: Arabic Alchemists Mapped Nitric Acid 600 Years Before Europe
description: While most people credit medieval Europe with the first record of nitric acid, Arabic scholars documented its preparation centuries earlier. Their recipes show a sophisticated understanding of the substance long before it appeared in European texts.
narration: NITRIC ACID IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You assume nitric acid first appears in 13th‑century European alchemy. In fact, Arabic texts from the 8th century already describe it as a distilled oil‑like liquid used in experiments. The 8th‑century Ṣundūq al‑ḥikma, linked to Jabir ibn Hayyan, lists a mixture of nitre, green vitriol and Yemen alum heated to produce an oil‑like liquid matching nitric acid. Holmyard and al‑Hassan cite this as the earliest description. Arabic alchemists brewed nitric acid centuries before Europe imagined its power.
